To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the secrecy performance of a system is improved if the side information is available at the decoder and not the encoder, and the performance is further improved if the side-information is available to all the decoders and the encoders are allowed to cooperate.
we have developed an achievable rate-distortion based region for a secrecy system with side-information at decoders.

We study the problem of lossy compression of a correlated source over a broadcast channel in which the decoders have access side information correlated with the source, and derive an achievable rate-distortion based region that depends on the correlation among the source, the side information, and the channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a rate-distortion based secure communication system in which the decoders have access side information sequences that may or may not be correlated.
the design of a secrecy system in which the decoders have access side information correlated with the source and the communication performance is evaluated under the rate-distortion framework.
the design of secrecy systems with side information at multiple decoders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the general case, the achievable region is not tight, and for the special cases the exact bounds are not tight, but they are tight in the high-rate region.
the side information sequences can be utilized in the Wyner Ziv setting to achieve better secrecy performance.
the secrecy system with side-information at the decoders can be viewed as a generalization of the Wyner-Zive problem, and it can be studied in a rate-distortion framework.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a framework for the design of secrecy systems with side information.
we have studied a rate-distortion based Wyner-Ziv type problem, with the additional constraint of secrecy.
the side information at the decoder can be used to improve both the distortion performance and the secrecy performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the secrecy performance of a system can be improved by introducing side information to the legitimate decoders.

, in the absence of any side information at the encoders, the rate-distortion region of the system with side information is the same as the region obtained by the Wyner-Zive problem with the same side information.
the secrecy performance of the proposed system can be improved significantly by exploiting side information.
